	Definitions:
	Household and non-profit institutions serving households final consumption expenditure (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: ABJR + HAYO)
	General government final consumption (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: NMRY)
	Total gross fixed capital formation (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: NPQT)
	Business investment (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.8, identifier: NPEL)
	Private sector investment in dwellings, including transfer costs (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.8, identifier: L636 + L637)
	General government gross fixed capital formation (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.8, identifier: DLWF)
	Public corporations investment in dwellings, including transfer costs (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.8, identifier: L634 + L635)
	Net acquisitions of valuables (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: NPJR)
	Final domestic demand is the sum of private consumption, government consumption, fixed investment and net acquisition of valuables
	Change in inventories (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: CAFU)
	Total domestic demand is the sum of final domestic demand and change in inventories
	Total exports (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: IKBK)
	Total final expenditure (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: ABMG)
	Total imports (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: IKBL)
	Statistical discrepancy GDP(E) (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: GIXS)
	Gross domestic product at market prices (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: ABMI)

	Definitions:
	Household and non-profit institutions serving households final consumption expenditure (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: ABJQ + HAYE)
	General government final consumption (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: NMRP)
	Total gross fixed capital formation (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: NPQS)
	General government investment (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.8, identifier: RPZG)
	Net acquisitions of valuables (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: NPJQ)
	Final domestic demand is the sum of private consumption, government consumption, fixed investment and net acquisition of valuables
	Change in inventories (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: CAEX)
	Total domestic demand is the sum of final domestic demand and change in inventories
	Total exports (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: IKBH)      
	Total final expenditure (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: ABMF)
	Total imports (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: IKBI)
	Statistical discrepancy GDP(E) (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: GIXM)
	Gross domestic product at market prices (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.2, identifier: YBHA)
	Gross national income at market prices (ONS Economic Accounts Table 1.1.1, identifier: ABMZ)

	Definitions:						Definitions:
	Per person LFS employment = LFS employment, all aged 16 and over (ONS identifier: MGRZ) divided by total population (ONS identifier: EBAQ)						Per person LFS employment = LFS employment, all aged 16 and over (ONS identifier: MGRZ) divided by LFS population, all aged 16 and over (ONS identifier: MGSL)
	Per person real household disposable income = Real household disposable income (chained volume measure, identifier: NRJR) divided by total population (ONS identifier: EBAQ)						Per person real household disposable income = Real household disposable income (chained volume measure, identifier: NRJR) divided by LFS population, all aged 16 and over (ONS identifier: MGSL)
	Per person real consumption = Household and non-profit institutions serving households final consumption expenditure (chained volume measure, identifier: ABJR+HAYO) divided by total population (ONS identifier: EBAQ)						Per person real consumption = Household and non-profit institutions serving households final consumption expenditure (chained volume measure, identifier: ABJR+HAYO) divided by LFS population, all aged 16 and over (ONS identifier: MGSL)
	Per person real GDP = Gross domestic product at market prices (chained volume measure, identifier: ABMI) divided by total population (ONS identifier: EBAQ)						Per person real GDP = Gross domestic product at market prices (chained volume measure, identifier: ABMI) divided by LFS population, all aged 16 and over (ONS identifier: MGSL)

	2031-32	35.43	60.62	30.57	1.53	4.14	63.24	31.69	1123	45.17	54.61	1852	1492	359.2	224.6	2.589	189.5	187.2	114	113.6	113.5	113.5	100.6	99.34
	Definitions:
	LFS employment, all aged 16 and over (ONS identifier: MGRZ)
	LFS employment rate, all aged 16 and over (ONS identifier: MGSR)
	LFS employees equal to total employment less self-employed, all aged 16 and over (ONS identifier: MGRZ less MGRQ)
	ILO unemployment, all aged 16 and over (ONS identifier: MGSC)
	ILO unemployment rate, all aged 16 and over (ONS identifier: MGSX)
	LFS participation rate, all aged 16 and over (ONS identifier: MGWG)
	LFS average (mean) actual weekly hours worked, all workers (ONS identifier: YBUV)
	LFS total weekly hours worked, millions (ONS identifier: YBUS). Estimates before 2019Q1 calculated from LFS average actual weekly hours worked (ONS identifier: YBUV) multiplied by LFS employment (ONS identifier: MGRZ)
	Labour income share: wages and salaries (ONS identifier: DTWM) and mixed income (ONS identifier: ROYH) as a share of nominal Gross Domestic Product (ONS identifier: YBHA).
	Labour compensation share: wages and salaries (ONS identifier: DTWM), employers social contributions (ONS identifier: ROYK) and mixed income (ONS identifier: ROYH) as a share of nominal Gross Domestic Product (ONS identifier: YBHA).
	Compensation of employees, £ billion (ONS identifier: DTWM)
	Wages and salaries, £ billion, equal to total compensation of employees (ONS identifier: DTWM) minus employers social contributions (ONS identifier: ROYK)
	Employers social contributions, £ billion (ONS identifier: ROYK)
	Average weekly earnings growth: wages and salaries divided by employees, year on year growth rates and index. Wages and salaries equal to total compensation of employees (ONS identifier: DTWM) minus employers social contributions (ONS identifier: ROYK).  Employees equal to total employment (MGRZ) less self-employed (MGRQ)
	Average hourly earnings index: average weekly earnings divided by average hours worked  (ONS identifier: YBUV) 
	Productivity per hour: real GDP (ONS identifier: ABMI) divided by total weekly hours worked (ONS identifier: YBUS)
	Productivity per worker index: real GDP (ONS identifier: ABMI) divided by total 16+ employment (ONS identifier: MGRZ)
	Real product wage index: Compensation of employees (ONS identifier: DTWM) divided by employees (total employment (MGRZ) less self-employed (MGRQ)) and then deflated by the Gross Valued Added deflator (GVA at current market prices (ONS identifier: ABML) divided by GVA chained volume measure (ABMM))
	Real consumption wage: Compensation of employees (ONS identifier: DTWM) divided by employees (total employment (MGRZ) less self-employed (MGRQ)) and then deflated by the consumer expenditure deflator (households final consumption expenditure at current market prices (ABJQ) plus non-profit institutions (HAYE) divided by households final consumption expenditure, chained volume measure (ABJR) plus non-profit institutions (HAYO))
	Real weekly earnings index: average weekly earnings divided by consumer price index (ONS identifier: D7BT )
	Real hourly earnings index: average hourly earnings divided by consumer price index (ONS identifier: D7BT )
	Note: Historical data from the ONS Labour Force Survey include the latest reweighted estimates published on 3 December 2024. This creates a discontinuity in the series between Q4 2018 and Q1 2019, with the exception of UK total employment, unemployment, inactivity, and participation.

	Notes:
	RPI, RPIX, CPI and CPIH inflation are based on outturn data up to and including July 2026.
	Consumer expenditure deflator and GDP deflator are based on the Quarterly National Accounts released by the ONS on 13 August 2026.
	Actual rents for housing’ component of CPI. This series is constructed using forecasts of social housing rents and private rents. 
	Definitions:
	All items Retail Prices Index (RPI), all items Retail Prices Index excluding mortgage interest payments (RPIX) (percentage change over 12 months) (ONS Consumer Prices Index Bulletin, identifier: CZBH and CDKQ respectively). Due to a change in methodology we will not forecast RPIX after 2029 Q4.
	All items Consumer Prices Index (CPI), All items Consumer Prices Index including owner occupiers' housing costs (CPIH), Owner occupiers' housing costs (OOH) (percentage change over 12 months) (ONS Consumer Prices Index Bulletin, identifier: D7G7, L55O, and L5P7 respectively)
	Mortgage Interest Payments (ONS Consumer Prices Index Statistical Bulletin, identifier: CZCR). Due to the announced change in RPI methodology by the ONS from February 2030 we do not forecast RPI Mortgage Interest Payments and RPIX after 2029 Q4.
	Actual rents for housing (ONS Consumer Prices Index Bulletin, identifier: D7GQ)
	Private rentals for housing (ONS Consumer Prices Index Bulletin, identifier: KYHJ)
	Consumer expenditure deflator: Households final consumption expenditure at current market prices (ABJQ) plus non-profit institutions (HAYE) divided by Households final consumption expenditure, chained volume measure (ABJR) plus non-profit institutions (HAYO)

	Definitions:
	Labour income = Employee compensation (including net compensation from abroad) + mixed income (largely self-employment income) - employer social contributions. (ONS Economic Accounts, identifier: DTWM+ROYH-ROYK+IJAH-IJAI)

	Net benefits and taxes = Social benefits (resource) - taxation on income and wealth - employees' social contributions (excluding employee contributions to funded pension schemes). (ONS Economic Accounts, identifier: RPHL-RPHS-RPHT-L8PS-L8Q8-L8LU + (L8PE+L8Q2+L8LQ) + (CX3X+FJBH)). 
	Household disposable income (ONS Economic Accounts, identifier: RPHQ)

	Definitions:
	OBR estimate of potential population, based on LFS household population, all aged 16 and over (ONS identifier: MGSL) 
	OBR estimate of the potential participation rate, on the same basis as the LFS participation rate, all aged 16 and over (ONS identifier: MGWG)
	OBR estimate of the equilibirum unemployment rate, on the same basis as the ILO unemployment rate, all aged 16 and over (ONS identifier: MGSX)
	OBR estimate of the potential employment rate, on the same basis as the LFS employment rate, all aged 16 and over (ONS identifier: MGSR)
	OBR estimate of potential average hours, on the same basis as LFS average (mean) actual weekly hours worked, all workers (ONS identifier: YBUV)
	OBR estimate of potential output per hour, on the same basis as GDP (ONS identifier: ABMI) divided by total weekly hours worked (ONS identifier: YBUS)
	Notes:
	1 Potential output can be calculated by multiplying potential population,  productivity, average hours and the employment rate divided by 100. 
	2 The potential employment rate is determined by multiplying the potential participation rate by 1 minus the equilibrium unemployment rate divided by 100. 
	3 Potential output growth is approximately equal to the sum of the growth rates of potential population, the employment rate, average hours and productivity.

	1.18 Eligible rent growth assumptions
			2025-26	2026-27	2027-28	2028-29	2023-30	2030-31	2031-32
	Private sector
	Local Housing Allowance		4.2	3.2	3.3	3	2.8	2.7	2.5
	Non-LHA Regulated		4	4	4	4	4	4	4
	Non-LHA Deregulated		4	4	4	4	4	4	4
	Social sector
	Local Authorities		7.5	4.6	4.9	5.5	3.9	3.9	3.7
	Registered Social Landlords		15.7	7.5	7.6	7.9	6.5	6.6	6.5
	Notes:
	The assumptions provided in this table cover only growth in the element of rent eligible for Housing Benefit and not overall market rents. The eligible rent is based on the amount paid by the tenant to occupy the property not including bills and some service charges. In many cases (mainly Private Rented Sector tenants), the amount of eligible rent is also influenced by the amount of maximum rent determined by LHA regulations, or by the Rent Officer.
	These figures now include compositional shifts, including the Move to UC, the increase in use of affordable tenancies and increases to Supported Housing caseloads.
	The assumptions provided in this table include the impact of social rent convergence. We assume that all cases in scope of convergence are below national formula rents for modelling purposes. Some cases may also converge earlier than is modelled, and therefore require smaller rent increases each financial year, decreasing the average rental growth.
